issues.title: Uganda declares itself free of Ebola as Congo continues to struggle with it
issues.summary: Ugandan authorities have declared the country free of Ebola after the last patient was discharged in mid-June. The outbreak was linked to a larger one in eastern Congo's Ituri province. The first cases in Uganda were Congolese people seeking treatment. Uganda confirmed two Ebola cases on May 15, the same day Congo declared its outbreak. The Ugandan Ministry of Health stated that all identified contacts were quarantined and completed a 21-day follow-up without further transmission. The Bundibugyo type of Ebola virus responsible for the outbreak has no approved vaccine or treatment.
